docs.title: Home
docs.text:
FJB Relaunch — FFXI Private Server

Fresh Start Server

Extreme QoL. Fast progression. No grind tax.

Hit 99 in an hour. Chase best-in-slot for months. This is FFXI the way it should feel.

The Relaunch is a fresh-start FFXI private server built around one idea: the grind should be fun, not a wall. We cut the mandatory busywork, kept the depth, and bolted on a custom endgame that gives you something real to chase — whether you've been playing for a week or a year.

New Player? Start here.

Don't know where to begin? The Getting Started guide walks you through installing the client, connecting to the server, and taking your first steps — in about 20 minutes.

Already playing? See what's new

The Changelog lists every recent update and balance change, newest first, grouped by week.

docs.title: What makes this server different
docs.text:
Retail FFXI is a masterpiece buried under 20 years of time-gating. Most private servers swing the other direction and trivialize everything. This server splits the difference:

  • Fast leveling, real endgame. 3× mob EXP (plus 10× from books, FoV/GoV & Records of Eminence) gets you to 99 in a few hours, not months. Then the actual game begins.
  • Everything unlocked at creation. Advanced jobs, all outpost warps, all maps, full inventory — no arbitrary gates.
  • Custom content built for long-term play. The Hunting League, Reforge gear, Ascension, and weekly objectives give you a loop that doesn't expire.
  • A small, friendly community. No drama, no gatekeeping — just people who like this game.

docs.title: Feature highlights
docs.text:
Hunting League — A custom 5-rank NM hunting system. Kill your way from Initiate to Legend, unlocking gear, titles, and HL Points at every tier.

Ascension — The endgame above the endgame. Reaching Legend opens a per-job, no-cap progression track: re-clear escalating superboss Courts to bank Ascension Points and spend them on permanent stat boosts. The gauntlet swaps to a deadlier roster every 10 ascensions, so the climb never goes stale.

Reforge system — Three parallel NM ladders (AF, Relic, Empy) that upgrade your armor from base all the way to +3. Best-in-slot is earnable, not bought.

Augment Moogle — 400+ augment options. Trade catalysts from NM kills to permanently customize your gear in ways retail never allowed.

Weekly Hunt Board — Five rotating objectives every week. Complete all five for a big bonus. Always something to do.

Wave Master — An NPC arena in Escha - Ru'Aun that spawns themed NM waves for solo or group practice. Earn Hunt Marks. Flex on your friends.

Hunter's Guild — Four hunting guilds that rank up as you kill their NMs, permanently boosting the marks every kill pays out. Hit Grandmaster across all of them for the Trinity and Apex Hunter titles.

Custom Trusts — Allies you won't find on retail: Gemma (a full healer / buffer / debuffer in a deceptively small package) and Meat (an unkillable wall that never drops aggro).

Living economy — The auction house is never empty: a market-maker keeps thousands of gear listings stocked around the clock — a built-in price floor and gil sink — so you can actually buy your upgrades.

Achievements & Leaderboards — 26 milestones that pay bonus marks and titles as you rack up first kills, tier climbs, and lifetime records — plus live server leaderboards (top hunters, fastest clears, most augments) to climb.

Adventuring Fellow — A personal companion any job can summon. It levels from your kills, and you build it by spending stat points however you like.

Voidwatch — Examine Planar Rifts scattered across 30 overworld zones, fight tier-scaled Voidwalker NMs, and probe their hidden weaknesses to shape your rewards.

docs.title: New character bonuses
docs.text:
Every new character starts with:

  • 5,000,000 Gil in your wallet
  • 80 inventory slots (the maximum)
  • All maps for every zone
  • All outpost warps already unlocked
  • Advanced jobs unlocked — no quest required
  • Subjob unlocked — use it at full level immediately

docs.title: What's waiting at endgame?
docs.text:
The real game starts at 99.

Most servers have nothing to do after you level cap. This server was built around that problem.

Hunting League (5 tiers) Progress through Initiate → Hunter → Elite → Champion → Legend by killing increasingly difficult NMs. Each tier unlocks stronger gear options, higher HL Point rates, and exclusive titles. The grind is real — and it's meant to be.

Ascension / Prestige (the layer above Legend) The true ceiling. Reaching Legend tier opens the Ascension Altar in Provenance — a per-job, infinite progression track. Defeat the Nightmare Court (three dread superbosses), pay an escalating Mark cost, and bank Ascension Points to permanently empower the job you're playing.

Hunter's Guild (4 guilds, lifetime amplifiers) A passive reputation layer on top of every NM track. Each guild — AF, Relic, Empyrean, and League — ranks up as you kill its NMs, permanently amplifying the marks you earn from that source. Push to Grandmaster across multiple guilds for the Trinity and Apex Hunter capstones.

Reforge Gear (+3 from NM kills) Three independent NM ladders — AF Marks from Sky Gods, Relic Marks from Unity NMs, Empy Marks from Abyssea NMs — each upgrades a full armor set from base to +1 to +2 to +3. No RNG. No gacha. Just kills.

Augment Moogle (400+ augment options) Catalysts drop from monsters across the world. Trade them to the Augment Moogle to permanently apply stat bonuses to your gear. Pair with the Augment Sage to push augment strength even further.

Voidwatch Examine Planar Rifts across 30 overworld zones to trigger tier-scaled Voidwalker NM fights. Probe hidden weaknesses with magic, weaponskills, and ranged attacks to light up Spectral Alignments and earn bigger rewards from the Riftworn Pyxis.

Adventuring Fellow Summon a personal companion on any job. It levels from your kills and you spend the points on the stats you choose — name it, pick its look, and bring it into every fight.

Weekly Hunt Board Five objectives, reset every week. Complete all five and you earn a significant bonus. Always rotating, never stale.

Daily Board Three fresh objectives every day, reset at UTC midnight. Clear all three in one day for a bonus on top.

Custom Trusts Summons you won't find on retail. Gemma heals, raises, buffs, debuffs, and magic-bursts your skillchains. Meat soaks every hit and refuses to let go of aggro. Both are 50M-gil permanent unlocks.

Achievements (26 milestones) Twenty-six personal milestones paying bonus Hunt Marks and titles, with the biggest ones triggering a server-wide announcement.

Leaderboards See where you rank across the server — most augments crafted, top hunters, fastest clears — pulled live from the database and refreshed regularly.

Think this sounds good? Get started now. Or read What's Custom for the full breakdown — and check the Changelog for the latest updates.

docs.title: Server Rules
docs.text: This is a small, friendly community. We have a short list of rules designed to keep it that way. None of this is complicated — just be a reasonable person and you'll be fine.

docs.title: The Short Version
docs.text:
• Cheating is frowned upon. Bots, automation, and packet editing are discouraged — play fair.
  • Be decent to people. Harassment isn't tolerated.
  • No real-money trading. Gil and items stay in-game. Period.
  • Don't exploit bugs. Found one? Report it. Don't farm it.
  • No account limits. Multi-box as much as you like.
  • GMs are not vending machines. They don't spawn items or content on request.

docs.title: Fair Play
docs.text:
Cheating is frowned upon. Third-party tools that automate gameplay — combat bots, AHK macros that play the game for you, and anything that removes the need for a human at the keyboard — go against the spirit of the server, and the community tends to look down on them.

Quality-of-life plugins through Windower or Ashita are fine — maps, chat filters, bag sorting, item tooltips. We're not interested in policing the things that make the game more playable.

Speedhacks, wallhacks, and packet editing fall into the same "frowned upon" bucket: they hand you an edge over people playing with just the game client, and that's not the kind of play we want to encourage. If you're unsure whether a tool crosses the line, ask in Discord.

docs.title: Economy
docs.text: No real-money trading. Gil and items exist in the game economy, not for sale outside of it. Selling or buying Gil for real money — or brokering item purchases with real currency — is a permanent ban, no appeal. This isn't about the letter of the rule; it's about keeping the game fair for people who actually play it.

docs.title: Multi-Boxing
docs.text: There are no account limits and no cap on how many characters you run at once. Multi-box freely — a single support character to buff your main, or a full party of your own, it's all fine. Playing multiple characters is a normal part of how a lot of people enjoy FFXI.

docs.title: Bug Reporting
docs.text:
Found a bug or an exploitable mechanic? Report it in the #bugs channel in Discord.

Using an exploit for personal gain before reporting it — especially one that affects the economy, spawn rates, or item acquisition — will result in strikes against your account. How many depends on severity.

Good-faith bug reports are welcomed and rewarded. We'd rather fix something than police it.

docs.title: Community Standards
docs.text:
No harassment, hate speech, slurs, or targeted toxicity. This is a small server — you'll be playing with the same people for months. Act accordingly.

Trash talk in competition is fine. Targeting someone to make them miserable is not. Staff use judgment; there's no exhaustive list of prohibited words.

docs.title: GMs and Staff
docs.text:
GMs are here for server maintenance, not customer service. They do not:

  • Give out items, Gil, or gear
  • Spawn content on demand
  • Intervene in normal competitive gameplay
  • Teleport you because you got stuck (use /heal or rezone)

If you see a GM online, they're doing maintenance. Staff will never ask for your account password or credentials. If someone claiming to be a GM asks for your password, that's an impersonator — report it immediately.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Most rule violations follow a three-strike process:

  1. Warning — you're told what you did and why it's a problem
  2. 24-hour ban — temporary removal from the server
  3. Permanent ban — account terminated

Severe violations — real-money trading, sustained harassment campaigns, large-scale exploiting — skip directly to permanent ban without warning. Staff judgment is final, but bans can be appealed in Discord.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
All reports, appeals, and questions go through Discord. Use the appropriate channel:

  • #bugs — bugs and exploits
  • #questions — general questions
  • #recommendations — suggestions and feature ideas
  • #general — everything else: Hall of Fame milestone submissions, and ban appeals or account issues (or DM a GM directly)

The goal is a fun server, not a perfectly policed one. Use good judgment, treat people well, and you'll never have to think about this page again.

docs.title: About the Relaunch
docs.text: This is a fresh-start server — a clean wipe and rebuild of the FJB FFXI private server, redesigned from the ground up for long-term play.

docs.title: Why a Relaunch?
docs.text:
The original server proved the concept: FFXI with fast progression, a custom endgame, and a friendly community works. Players stayed for months. But over time, the economy inflated, veteran characters pulled far ahead of newcomers, and the gap between a day-one player and a year-one player became difficult to close.

The Relaunch fixes that. Everyone starts equal. The economy is fresh. The stat balance has been redesigned from scratch. And the content lineup has been expanded with systems that weren't in the original — Voidwatch, the Adventuring Fellow, Boom Job, Spell & Skill Mastery, and more.

docs.title: What's Different from the Original
docs.text:
Redesigned stats and mob balance. Enemy stats have been rebuilt from the ground up so that gear choices, skill investment, and build decisions all actually matter. The power curve is tighter and more deliberate.

New relaunch-exclusive systems. The Relaunch ships content that was never on the original server:

  • Voidwatch — Planar Rifts scattered across 30 overworld zones, tier-scaling Voidwalker NM fights, and a Spectral Alignment reward system
  • Adventuring Fellow — a personal companion any job can summon, leveled and built by the player
  • Boom Job — a custom job on the Summoner slot: a staff-swinging hybrid DD whose spells randomly detonate
  • Spell & Skill Mastery — permanent WS and spell power-ups earned from a rotating NM currency system
  • Affinity NM timed spawns — all 24 Augment Sage affinity NMs placed as real timed spawns in their zones

A living economy from day one. The auction house market-maker seeds gear listings immediately at launch — no waiting months for the economy to bootstrap.

docs.title: What Carried Over
docs.text:
Everything that made the original server worth playing:

  • Fast progression, real endgame. 3× mob EXP (and 10× from books, FoV/GoV & Records of Eminence) means you hit 99 in days, not months. But 99 is the beginning, not the finish line. The Hunting League, Reforge gear, augments, and a full tier of endgame events are all designed to hold your interest for months. There's always a next thing.

  • Hunting League — a custom 5-tier progression system. Retail FFXI has NMs. Legendary turns them into a structured progression ladder. Five ranks, each harder than the last, each with meaningful rewards and increasing HL Point rates. If you love the hunt, this server was built for you.

  • Ascension — a prestige ladder above the level cap. Reach the Hunting League's Legend tier and the Altar in Provenance opens. Re-clear the Nightmare Court — three ascension-only superbosses that get harder and change as you climb — and spend Hunt Marks to ascend, earning Ascension Points: a Job-Points-style currency poured into permanent, stacking stat boosts. It's tracked per main job, never wipes anything you've earned, and the prestige levels are uncapped — an endless Paragon tail to chase on the leaderboards. Its per-job sibling, Job Rebirth, resets a mastered job to level 1 to bank permanent Rebirth Points.

  • Reforge system — three NM ladders to +3 BiS. Kill Sky Gods for AF Marks. Kill Unity NMs for Relic Marks. Kill Abyssea NMs for Empy Marks. Each currency line upgrades a full armor set across four tiers. No RNG boxes, no cash shop — just the satisfaction of killing your way to best-in-slot.

  • Hunter's Guild — reputation that pays you back. Four hunting guilds, each tied to one of the mark currencies, are climbed by tracking down classic HNMs scattered across Vana'diel — not by farming the spawners. Every rank you earn passively amplifies the marks that currency pays out, so the more of the world you hunt, the faster your Reforge and Hunting League grinds go. Reach Grandmaster across multiple guilds and the Trinity and Apex meta-bonuses unlock.

  • Augment Moogle — 400+ ways to customize your gear. Catalysts drop from monsters all over the world. Trade them to the Augment Moogle to apply permanent stat bonuses to your gear. Stack them with the Augment Sage (whose power scales with your NM kill history) and you can push gear further than retail ever allowed.

  • Cross-Job Abilities — borrow from other jobs. The Cross-Job Trainer in GM Home sells a hand-curated set of job abilities — self and party buffs and utility, like Meditate — that you can then use on any job via macro, with the recast enforced server-side. No 2-hours, no build-breaking picks: just the smart cross-pollination retail never allowed.

  • No dead content — weekly objectives, daily board, Wave Master arena. The Weekly Hunt Board resets every week with five fresh objectives. The Daily Board resets at midnight UTC. The Wave Master NPC in Escha - Ru'Aun spawns NM waves on demand. There is always a reason to log in.

  • Endgame & Events — a whole tier of things to do at 99. Take on The Star-Devourer, a weekly multi-phase raid boss; climb the endless Voidspire gauntlet for a leaderboard floor; duel level-scaled champions in the Colosseum; hold the line against scheduled Invasions; dig up buried Treasure; bet at the Chocobo Derby; rank up the fishing-and-crafting Provisioners' League; or push your luck at Lady Luck's Casino — plus rotating Seasonal Events that supercharge your hunts.

  • Prime Armory — claim an apex Prime weapon. Trade a Prime Voucher at the Prime Armory for one of twelve Prime weapons, the server's top weapon tier. Browse the full set in the menu and take the one built for your job.

  • Achievements & World Firsts. Hit a personal milestone and you bank bonus Hunt Marks plus an in-game shout-out. Be the first on the server to pull something off and everyone hears about it — world-first announcements give the race to the top real stakes.

  • Leaderboards — see where you rank. The Chronicler at Reisenjima Henge tallies your kills, unique NMs, and competitive stats, and a live website ranks every player server-wide, refreshed from the database through the day. Whether you're chasing Paragon levels or the longest hunt streak, there's always a scoreboard watching.

  • A deep quality-of-life bench. Always-popped NMs (no camping, no lottery), a Character Upgrader that hands a new character everything in one click, homepoint healing, zone-in cutscene skips, sub-job EXP share, gil-sink vendors, seasonal events, login streaks — dozens of friction-removers, all catalogued on the Quality of Life Features page.

  • Everything unlocked at character creation. No quest to unlock advanced jobs. No tour of outpost warps. No waiting for maps. You create a character and immediately have access to everything that retail made you spend weeks unlocking. The friction that doesn't make the game better is just gone.

Ready to start?

The Getting Started guide will have you in-game in about 20 minutes. Everything else you need is in these docs.

docs.title: Custom HNM system
docs.text:
the Relaunch server runs a hybrid HNM pop system that blends era-style timed rotation with retail-style QM pops:

  • NQ kings (Fafnir, Behemoth, Aspidochelone, etc.) rotate on a timed window, persisting across server restarts.
  • HQ kings (Nidhogg, King Behemoth, etc.) drop via QM placeholders.
  • Respawn timers persist across restarts — crashes don't reset the clock.
  • Each king's respawn window is tuned individually (e.g. Fafnir's is 21–24h).

docs.title: World-first announcements
docs.text:
The server broadcasts to everyone online when a milestone is first achieved:

  • First player death (server-wide bragging rights)
  • First level-up to each level per job (e.g. "First WAR to hit 75")
  • First NM kills for tracked HNMs
  • Winners are recorded permanently, so the title stays attributed even after restarts.

docs.title: Background systems
docs.text:
System-level modules that change behavior server-wide without adding NPCs. You probably won't notice them directly — but you'll notice their absence on a vanilla server.

Module What it changes Always-Popped NMs Every NM in Abyssea (all 10 zones), Escha (Zi'Tah + Ru'Aun), Reisenjima, and Reisenjima Sanctorium auto-spawns at server start and respawns 30 seconds after death. No trade pop, no key item, no atmacite, no cruor — just walk in and fight. HNMs and wave bosses included. Reisenjima Henge is excluded so the Hunting League's on-demand spawner can keep working. Unlimited Visitant (Abyssea) Every player gets permanent Visitant status the moment they zone into any Abyssea area. No timer, no eject to Searing Ward, no pearl/atma farming just to stay alive. Same mechanism retail uses for GMs, applied to everyone. Homepoint Heal Every homepoint visit restores full HP & MP. No more relying on a healer at the crystal. Persistent NM Time of Death NM respawn timers survive crashes and restarts. Currently tracks Behemoth (21–24h window), with more NMs addable. Disable Zone-In Cutscenes Suppresses every auto-cutscene that fires when you zone into an area with a mission/quest stage that would normally trigger one. Side effects (position resets, charvar updates, key item grants) still happen — only the cutscene playback is skipped. Talk to the NPC manually if you want to see it. Auto Unstick Server-side watchdog that clears stuck event state from any character on zone-in. If your character is wedged in a "still in cutscene" state, just zone (or log out and back in) and the watchdog releases you. Also defuses the Mog House 2F unlock cutscene loop that traps some characters. Conquest Regional NPCs Always Up Bastok, Windurst, and San d'Oria regional NPCs stay visible regardless of which nation owns conquest. No "come back next week" walls. Mission Wardrobe Unlocks Hitting mission milestones unlocks Mog Wardrobe slots. Currently: Zilart completion → Mog Wardrobe 3 unlocked. Max-Size Mog Wardrobes at Creation All 8 Mog Wardrobes are pre-sized to maximum capacity on character creation. By default, wardrobes 1-8 start at 0 slots until manually expanded; this skips that and gives every new character full storage from minute one. New Player Linkshell New characters automatically receive a designated server linkshell at character creation. Login Announcements Broadcasts a server-wide message when a player logs in, so the community knows when familiar names are online. First-99 Timestamp Tracker The first time any of a character's jobs hits level 99, the timestamp is stamped permanently into a charvar. Powers the "Fastest 1 → 99" leaderboard on the Community page. Lock-once — re-leveling another job to 99 doesn't overwrite the stamp. Chocobo Raising QoL Faster chocobo growth (2 days to chick stage), higher endgame stat caps (riding speed 120, endurance), tuned for active raising. Wish Upon a Star Workaround Patches the Bastok "Wish Upon a Star" weather-gate quest that's otherwise impossible without a specific weather event. SoA Imprimatur Gate Removed Seekers of Adoulin missions no longer require Imprimatur key items or fame. Talk to the NPC, get the mission. Garrison Placeholder Data Supplies temporary NPC appearance data (looks, weapons) for Garrison content so it runs even without captured units. Organized by level cap × nation.

  • Enmity cap (30,000)
  • Sneak/Invis/Deodorize durations
  • Old cure formula / old magic damage (both off — uses modern formulas)

docs.title: Background Systems
docs.text:
These are server-level systems that run silently in the background — no NPC to talk to, no command to type. Most players encounter them indirectly: you zone into Abyssea and an NM is already up, or you get stuck in a cutscene loop and zoning out fixes it.

This page explains what each system does so you know what's happening when you run into it.

docs.title: Abyssea Always-Popped
docs.text:
Every NM across all ten Abyssea zones, Escha (Zi'Tah + Ru'Aun), Reisenjima, and Reisenjima Sanctorium auto-spawns at server start and respawns 30 seconds after death.

No pop requirements. No trade items. No key items. No atmacite. No cruor threshold. Just walk in and start fighting.

This covers HNMs and wave bosses in those zones as well. If you're looking for a specific Abyssea NM, it's already up — or it'll be back in half a minute.

Reisenjima Henge excluded

The Henge itself is excluded from the always-pop system so the Hunting League's on-demand Spawner keeps working correctly.

docs.title: Unlimited Visitant
docs.text:
In retail Abyssea, Visitant status has a time limit — your clock ticks down, and when it runs out you get ejected. On this server, every player receives permanent Visitant status the moment they zone into any Abyssea area.

No timer. No decay. No atma farming just to stay inside. Zone in and stay as long as you want.

docs.title: Auto-Unstick
docs.text:
A server-side watchdog clears stuck event state whenever you zone in. If your character is locked in a cutscene loop or stuck in a "still in event" state, the fix is simple:

  1. Zone out (walk to a zone line, or use any teleport command).
  2. Zone back in.
  3. The watchdog fires on zone-in and releases the stuck state.

Tip

If zoning once doesn't clear it, log out and back in — that's a full zone-in cycle and always triggers the watchdog.

docs.title: Zone-In Cutscenes Disabled
docs.text:
Auto-cutscenes that fire when you zone into a mission-heavy area are suppressed. If you've ever had the game lock you into a five-minute cutscene just because you walked through a zone line, you know why this exists.

Any side effects that the cutscene would have produced — position resets, charvar updates, key item grants — still happen. Only the video playback is skipped.

If you want to watch a specific cutscene, talk to the relevant NPC manually.

docs.title: World-First Announcements
docs.text:
When a player achieves a server-first milestone, the server broadcasts it to everyone online. Tracked milestones include:

  • First player death on the server (yes, this one is tracked)
  • First level-up to 99 per job (e.g., "First WAR to hit 99")
  • First kills of tracked HNMs

These are stored permanently — a title stays attributed to the correct player even after server restarts. If you're racing for a world-first, everyone will know when it happens.

docs.title: Chocobo Raising
docs.text:
Chocobo raising is tuned for faster results:

  • 2-day chick cycle (faster than retail)
  • Higher stat caps — riding speed up to 120, higher endurance ceiling
  • Active raising is balanced around the faster growth curve

If you want a high-stat mount, raising is worth the investment.

docs.title: SoA Imprimatur Gate Removed
docs.text:
Seekers of Adoulin missions no longer require Imprimatur currency or fame to progress. Just talk to the NPC and accept the mission.

If you've ever hit the Imprimatur wall on retail (or on a standard private server), this won't be a problem here.

docs.title: Conquest Regional NPCs Always Up
docs.text:
Bastok, Windurst, and San d'Oria regional NPCs are permanently visible, regardless of which nation holds conquest standing in each region.

On retail, regional NPCs disappear when their nation loses the region — leaving you to come back next week. On this server, they're always there.

docs.title: Double-Duration Enhancing Magic
docs.text:
Every Enhancing Magic spell lasts twice as long as it normally would. The 2× is applied on top of all the usual modifiers — gear "Enhancing Magic Duration", RDM merits and job points, Composure, Perpetuance, and Embolden all stack first, then the result is doubled.

  • A 5-minute Protect becomes 10 minutes.
  • A Composure'd 5-minute buff (already ×3) becomes 30 minutes.

No NPC, no gear requirement — it applies to every player casting any enhancing spell.

docs.title: Blue Mage Auto-Learns Spells
docs.text:
Blue Mage never has to hunt down and learn spells the hard way. As your BLU levels up, every spell it would normally have to learn from a monster is granted automatically at the appropriate level. Logging in also runs a full catch-up, so a BLU is always holding the complete spell list for its current level.

You still set and arrange your own spells — this only removes the chore of farming each one off a mob.

docs.title: Auto-Buff at the Hunting League Hub
docs.text:
Zone into Escha - Zi'Tah (the Hunting League hub, reached with !hunt) and the server applies your buffs automatically — the same package as the !buff command: a regional buff plus Refresh, Regen, and Regain, for 30 minutes.

You can start hunting the moment you arrive without typing anything. If the buffs drop mid-session, !buff re-applies them anywhere.

docs.title: Al Zahbi Loot Fountain
docs.text: Every monster killed in Al Zahbi drops one extra random item, rolled from across the whole item database, on top of its normal loot. It is pure novelty — you never know what you'll get — and it stacks with the Scheduled Invasions that also take place there.

docs.title: GM Home Seal Drops
docs.text:
Monsters killed inside GM Home (where the Test Dummy lives) drop gear-vendor seals every kill — the currency the Gear Vendors accept. The seal tier scales with the mob's level, NMs drop a tier higher, and the quantity varies per kill (with the occasional jackpot stack). It's a small bonus faucet for testing your damage on something that fights back.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Common questions about playing on the Relaunch server FFXI. If you have a question that isn't answered here, ask in our Discord or open an issue on the project repo.

docs.title: How do I connect to the server?
docs.text: See Getting Started → Install the Client and Connect to Server for the full walkthrough.

docs.title: Do I need a Square Enix account or game license?
docs.text: No. the Relaunch server runs against a private server built on LandSandBoat. You only need the FFXI client itself, not an active SE subscription.

docs.title: How do I create a character?
docs.text: Once connected, the standard FFXI character-creation flow runs as usual. Every new character starts at the configured starting level, full inventory, all maps + outpost warps, and the starting gil bundle listed on the home page.

docs.title: Why does my character feel weak compared to retail at the same level?
docs.text: Stats are tuned for this server's faster progression curve, but combat is balanced around the level-99 cap with rebalanced gear. If you feel weak, check the Gear Vendors page — the Hunt Mark currencies are the fastest path to iLvl 119 gear.

docs.title: How do I earn Hunt Marks?
docs.text: Kill the NMs at the Hunting League Spawner. Each NM gives points scaled by tier; higher tiers give more. Unlock tiers using the Hub NPC at the hunt zone.

docs.title: What's the difference between the Hunting League NPC and the Reforge System NPC?
docs.text:
• Hunting League — entry-to-mid-tier gear sold for Hunt Marks (Bronze/Silver/Gold seals).
  • Reforge System — AF/Relic/Empyrean reforge upgrades. Drops base pieces + currency by killing categorized NMs (Sky Gods → AF Marks, Unity NMs → Relic Marks, Abyssea NMs → Empyrean Marks).

docs.title: How does the Augment Moogle differ from the Augment Sage?
docs.text:
• Augment Moogle stamps a single augment from a catalyst item onto a piece of gear. One catalyst, one augment.
  • Augment Sage is a rank system that multiplies augment values (up to 5× at top rank) plus per-NM affinity bonuses. Talk to the Sage to track and rank up.

docs.title: Where's the full list of player commands?
docs.text: Reference → Player Commands — every player command, with parameter types and descriptions. Each is tagged upstream or custom so you can tell which are server-specific.

docs.title: What does !mystats show me?
docs.text: A complete dump of every stat your character has, including bonuses from gear and active buffs. Useful for verifying that a piece of gear is actually doing what its tooltip says. See the !mystats entry for the full output format.

docs.title: Can I auto-spend job points / merits?
docs.text: Yes — !autojp and !automerits. Both spread points breadth-first across categories on your current main job, so no single category gets maxed before others get a look-in. See !autojp and !automerits.

docs.title: How do I find other players?
docs.text:
• Leaderboards — top players by Hunt Marks, NM kills, lifetime currency earned.
  • Player Profiles — browse individual character pages.
  • Discord — live chat, group-up posts, server announcements.

docs.title: Can I play solo?
docs.text: Yes. Almost all custom content (Hunting League, Reforge System, Weekly Hunts) can be soloed at the cap. Difficulty is gear-checked, not group-size-checked.

docs.title: The server's down / I can't connect. What do I do?
docs.text:
1. Check the Discord #server-status channel first — outages and maintenance windows are announced there.
  2. If the server is up but you can't connect, verify your client is pointed at the right login server (see Connect to Server).

docs.title: I think I found a bug. Where do I report it?
docs.text: Two options: - GitHub Issues — preferred for reproducible bugs with clear steps. - Discord #bug-reports — for quick reports or "is this intended?" questions.

docs.title: My character got stuck / I lost an item / something broke. Can a GM help?
docs.text: Ping a GM in Discord. Specify your character name, what happened, and roughly when. Most stuck-character and accidental-deletion situations can be resolved.

docs.title: What's different about this server vs. retail / vs. plain LandSandBoat?
docs.text:
The What's Custom page is the authoritative list. Highlights:

  • Faster EXP / CP / drop rates (current multipliers shown on the home page)
  • Full subjob from character creation
  • 99 starting level cap, all maps + outpost warps granted at creation
  • Custom Hunting League, Reforge System, Augment Sage, Player Trusts, and Weekly Hunt Board systems
  • Every player command listed in Reference → Player Commands

docs.title: Are character files / progress safe? Are there backups?
docs.text:
Yes — daily backups of the character database are taken. In a worst case, the most you'd lose is a few hours.

Have a question that should be on this page? Ping a GM in Discord and we'll add it.

docs.title: This Week's Featured Hunt
docs.text:
Each week a single NM per Hunting League tier is designated as the Featured Hunt. The first kill of that NM during the ISO week awards 2× Hunt Marks on top of the normal reward — a meaningful bonus for players who coordinate around it.

The Featured Hunt rotates automatically at the start of each ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC). To see which NMs are currently featured, use the in-game command:

!featured

First-Kill Bonus

The 2× marks apply to the first kill only per week. After that, the NM still drops normal marks — it never goes dry. Clear it early for the bonus, then keep farming.

docs.title: Active Events
docs.text:
Seasonal bonus-mark events multiply the Hunt Marks you earn from kills for a limited window. Only one applies at a time — if two overlap, the higher-priority one wins. For the live bonus, use !events in-game.

No bonus-mark events are active or scheduled right now. Watch #announcements on Discord for the next one.

Event Announcements

Seasonal events — including double-marks weekends and holiday content — are announced in the #announcements channel on Discord before going live. Keep an eye there for upcoming events.

docs.title: Cosmetic Boutique — Boutique Moogle
docs.text:
Want to stand out in town? The Boutique Moogle in GM Home runs a daily-rotating fashion shop — one appearance-only cosmetic per day, from festival yukatas to full monster costumes. No stats, pure glamour.

Summary

A new cosmetic is featured every day (resets 00:00 UTC). Examine the item in the shop window to see the look, then buy it with Allied Notes. Miss one? It comes back around as the rotation cycles.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• One featured cosmetic per day, rotating through the whole pool below (UTC reset).
  • Opens the native shop window — examine the icon to preview the piece before you buy.
  • Appearance only — cosmetics carry no combat stats.
  • Paid in Allied Notes (earned in Adoulin (S) zones).

docs.text:

docs.title: Gil Exchange — turning gil into Hunt Marks
docs.text:
Sitting on more gil than you'll ever spend? The Gil Exchange in GM Home converts raw gil into Hunt Marks, the currency that drives the Hunting League. The rates are deliberately steep — this is a last-resort sink for rich players, not a shortcut around hunting.

Summary

A gil sink in GM Home that buys Hunt Marks with your spare gil at intentionally poor rates — for players drowning in gil who still want progression.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Gil Exchange is in the gil-services row at GM Home. Speak to it to open the menu — your current gil shows at the top, and your Hunt Mark total is confirmed after each trade.

docs.title: Exchange bundles
docs.text:
Each bundle is a single click that spends gil for Hunt Marks. Bigger bundles give a slightly better ratio:

You pay You receive Rate 100k gil 1 Hunt Mark 100,000 gil each 1M gil 12 Hunt Marks 83,333 gil each 10M gil 150 Hunt Marks 66,667 gil each

Hunting NMs is still by far the fastest way to earn marks — think of this as a way to put a runaway gil pile to work, not a replacement for the hunt.

docs.title: Home Point Network — GM Home
docs.text:
A Home Point crystal stands in GM Home that works like a full home-point terminal: set your home point here, then free-warp to home points all across Vana'diel — no attunement, no gil, no gates.

Summary

A Home Point crystal in GM Home. Set your home point there and warp, for free, to home points across the whole world — every major city, the Adoulin and Aht Urhgan regions, the past, Sky, Sea, and dozens of dungeons and fields.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Home Point crystal sits in GM Home, in the travel-NPC cluster on the east side — alongside the other warp services. Using it is always free: no gil cost and no attunement, so every destination is open from your first visit.

docs.title: Setting your home point
docs.text: Choose Set home point here and GM Home becomes your home point — you'll return here whenever you're knocked out and raised, or any time you use a home-point warp. It also registers GM Home as a destination on the wider home-point network, so other crystals out in the world can send you back.

docs.title: Where you can warp
docs.text:
Talk to the crystal, choose Warp to a home point, pick a region, then pick a destination. Long regions are split across pages — use the Next and Prev buttons to scroll.

The crystal reaches 121 home points spread across 12 regions — effectively the entire home-point network in one place:

Region Home points San d'Oria 11 Bastok 12 Windurst 15 Jeuno 10 Aht Urhgan 5 Adoulin 4 Ulbuka 7 Other Towns 10 Past [S] 6 Sky 6 Sea 5 Dungeons & Fields 30 Total 121

docs.title: Race Changer
docs.text:
Want a fresh look? The Race Changer in GM Home lets you change your character's race and pick a new face for a flat gil fee. It's purely cosmetic and applies instantly — your level, jobs, and progress are untouched.

Summary

Pay a one-time gil fee at the Race Changer in GM Home to switch your race and face — instant, cosmetic, and nothing else about your character changes.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Race Changer stands at the end of the gil-services row in GM Home. Talk to it, choose a new race and face, then confirm.

docs.title: What it costs and what you get
docs.text:
A race change costs 100M gil (100,000,000 gil), charged once when you confirm. You can switch to any of the 8 races (your current one is left off the list) and pick from 16 faces per race. The change is instant and purely cosmetic — your size, level, jobs, and everything else stay exactly as they were.

Once you confirm, the fee is charged and you rezone for a moment so your new model loads. Any gear your new race can't wear is simply unequipped — pop it back on afterward.

docs.title: Reforge Mark Exchange
docs.text:
The Reforge Exchange lets you convert spare Reforge marks from one line into another, so a surplus you've banked in one track can fund the set you're actually upgrading.

Summary

Trade excess AF, Relic, or Empyrean marks for the line you need at the Reforge Exchange near the Gear Vendors — a small conversion tax keeps each track honest.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Reforge Exchange stands at Gwora-Corridor, right beside the Gear Vendors — the same spot where you turn marks into upgrades.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: The Reforge System runs three parallel upgrade tracks — AF, Relic, and Empyrean — and each track earns and spends its own marks. Hunt long enough and you'll bank far more marks in one track than you can use while another sits short. This NPC lets you rebalance that surplus toward the set you're chasing.

docs.title: Conversions
docs.text:
Each conversion charges a small tax, so trading down a surplus costs you a little but never trivializes a track:

You spend You receive Rate 2 AF Marks 1 Relic Marks 2:1 2 Relic Marks 1 Empy Marks 2:1 3 AF Marks 1 Empy Marks 3:1

docs.title: How to trade
docs.text:
Talk to the NPC and the menu lists each conversion with how many marks you currently hold. Pick a conversion, choose a batch size, and confirm — your source marks are spent and the new marks are added on the spot.

Each visit you can convert in batches of 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 target marks at once (you'll only be offered batches you can afford), so a large surplus can be moved over in a few clicks.

docs.title: Abyssea NMs — Hunt Marks System
docs.text:
Abyssea is home to some of the most powerful Notorious Monsters on the server. Rather than hunting down rare key items to spawn them, the Relaunch server replaces the retail pop system with a Hunt Marks spend: find the ???, pay your marks, and the NM rises right in front of you.

Summary

Spend Hunt Marks at any Abyssea ??? to pop its NM on demand. Kill it with your party for a large Infamy and Gil payout — no key items required.

docs.title: Zones & Difficulty Tiers
docs.text:
Abyssea is divided into three difficulty tiers based on the expansion each zone belongs to. Higher tiers demand more coordination, hit harder, and reward more.

Tier Zones Mark Cost Level HP Visions Konschtat, Tahrongi, La Theine 200 marks 135 500,000 Scars Attohwa, Misareaux, Vunkerl 350 marks 145 1,000,000 Heroes Altepa, Grauberg, Uleguerand 500 marks 155 1,900,000

These are not solo targets

All tiers are tuned for a full party of real players. Each NM has dramatically boosted ATK, DEF, accuracy, and evasion on top of its level-scaled stats. Coming in underprepared or alone is likely to end badly.

docs.title: Getting There
docs.text:
Use the !abyssea command to open a zone warp menu:

!abyssea

A two-tier menu appears — pick the expansion tier, then the specific zone. You'll land at a safe camp near the zone entrance.

docs.title: Popping an NM
docs.text:
Each Abyssea NM has a ??? landmark somewhere in the zone. Walk up to it and check:

If you're missing the retail key items (which you almost certainly are — they've been removed from the game):

  1. A menu appears showing the NM name and the Hunt Mark cost.
  2. If you have enough marks, a Pop button is available — confirm it.
  3. Your marks are spent, the NM spawns directly next to you, and it's already claimed to your party.

If you somehow still have the original retail key items, the vanilla pop still works — the ??? will handle it as normal.

Key items from retail

If you had any Abyssea pop key items from retail (Tattered Hippogryph Wing, Cracked Wivre Horn, etc.), they were automatically removed from your inventory when you last logged in. They have no function on this server.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text: Killing a marks-popped NM pays out Infamy and Gil to every member of your party. The payout scales with your party composition.

docs.title: Base rewards by tier
docs.text: Tier Infamy Gil Visions 25 250,000 Scars 40 500,000 Heroes 60 750,000

docs.title: Multipliers
docs.text:
Two bonuses can stack on top of the base reward:

Condition Multiplier 2 or more real players in party ×2.0 No trusts in party ×1.5

These multiply together, so a full party of real players with no trusts earns ×3.0.

docs.title: Full reward table
docs.text:
VisionsScarsHeroes Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 25 250,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 37 375,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 50 500,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 75 750,000 Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 40 500,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 60 750,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 80 1,000,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 120 1,500,000 Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 60 750,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 90 1,125,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 120 1,500,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 180 2,250,000

After the kill a system message confirms your payout and any active multiplier bonus.

docs.title: Superior Lv5 weapon drops (any mob)
docs.text:
Beyond the NMs, every regular mob in an Abyssea zone has a 5% chance on death to drop a Superior Lv5 (Dynamis Divergence) weapon into the treasure pool — a random one of the 22 below (one per job), free for the whole alliance to lot. No ???, pop, Hunt Marks, or trade required; just grind Abyssea mobs.

docs.title: What to Spend Infamy On
docs.text:
Infamy is spent at the Infamy Vendor in GM Home. The full catalog includes accessories, armor, Relic/Mythic/Aeonic weapons, and more. A few reference points:

Item tier Cost Accessories (Fotia Belt, earrings, rings) 250–300 Infamy Armor pieces (Nyame, Jhakri) 400–800 Infamy Relic / Aeonic weapons 800 Infamy Mythic weapons 10,000 Infamy

A party running Heroes NMs without trusts earns 180 Infamy per kill — enough for a full Nyame body in under 5 kills, and a Mythic weapon in roughly 55 kills.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Bring a healer. Every NM tier is designed to require active healing. The stat boosts are large enough that an undefended party member can be killed in a few hits.
  • Drop your trusts before the kill. The ×1.5 no-trust multiplier is free Infamy. Dismiss them once the NM is engaged and you're confident in your party.
  • The NM respawns after a server restart. If you pop and kill an NM, the ??? is available immediately for the next pop — there's no lockout timer.
  • You need to be the one to land the kill. Only parties where someone gets the killing blow trigger the reward. Don't let a rogue trust finish it off right as you dismiss them.

docs.title: Apex Trials & Paragon
docs.text:
Summary

Hit the cap and ran out of mountains to climb? Apex Trials is an infinite, scaling solo gauntlet that banks Paragon Points, which you spend at the Paragon Sage on an endless prestige track, permanent (capped) perks, and a daily buff. Your deepest Apex tier and your Paragon Level are both on the leaderboards — the first numbers on the server with no ceiling.

docs.title: Apex Trials
docs.text:
Apex Trials is an infinite, scaling solo climb — the one chase on the server with no summit. Talk to the Apex Arbiter in GM Home (the endgame row, beside the Prime Armory) or type !apex to begin.

Each tier pits you against a single scaled Apex boss (Apex Devourer, Paragon Sentinel, Ascendant Tyrant…). Clear it and you bank Paragon Points and raise your record, then the next tier spawns automatically — a little tougher. Keep climbing until you die or leave; the run ends, but every Paragon Point you banked on the way up is kept. Your next run resumes one tier above your record.

The first boss is around level 165 — a step above the toughest Hunting League NMs — and it only goes up from there. Walk of Echoes rules apply: solo (no Trusts), but your pets work.

docs.title: How the climb scales
docs.text:
A taste of the curve (difficulty climbs forever — level is capped at 230, after which HP and stats carry it):

Tier Boss level Boss HP Paragon Points (first clear) 1 165 1,100,000 10 5 181 1,793,520 30 10 201 3,304,446 55 20 230 11,217,165 105 30 230 38,077,422 155 50 230 438,769,484 255

HP multiplies by ×1.13 per tier, and the boss also gains roughly +450 Attack / +380 Defense / +70 Accuracy / +50 Evasion per tier on top.

docs.title: Affixes & Paragon Points
docs.text:
From tier 5 on, each boss rolls an extra affix every 5 tiers (up to 6 stacked at once), drawn from: Fortified, Frenzied, Regenerating, Empowered, Vampiric, Furious. Affixes also intensify the deeper you go.

Paragon Points banked for a new tier = 10 + 5 × (tier − 1) — and each tier only ever pays out once (your record only goes up), so it's pure push-your-record, never a farm.

Commands

!apex — show your record and unspent points · !apex enter — begin a climb (same as the NPC) · !apex abort — end your current climb (banked points are kept).

docs.title: Paragon
docs.text: Paragon is the meta-progression Apex Trials feeds. Spend the Paragon Points you bank at the Paragon Sage in GM Home (next to the Apex Arbiter) on three things: an infinite Paragon Level prestige track, permanent capped perks, and the Daily Might buff. It's deliberately flex-and-flavour — the perk caps are modest next to maxed gear, so Paragon is a prestige climb, not a power treadmill.

docs.title: Perks
docs.text:
Permanent stat boosts, applied automatically every time you log in or zone. Each has 10 ranks; the cap is reached at max rank:

Perk Boosts Per rank Cap (max rank) Vigor Max HP +500 +5,000 Might Attack & Ranged Attack +100 +1,000 Precision Accuracy & Ranged Accuracy +100 +1,000 Warding Defense +200 +2,000

docs.title: Paragon Levels & titles
docs.text:
Ascending from Paragon Level N to N+1 costs 25 + 5 × N Paragon Points — an endless prestige track that shows on !reallevel and the leaderboards. Your Paragon Level earns a scaling title:

Paragon Level Title 0 Aspirant 1+ Paragon 25+ Ascendant 50+ Eternal 100+ Voidlord

docs.title: Daily Might
docs.text:
Unlock Daily Might once for 80 Paragon Points, then claim it from the Paragon Sage once per day. It grants a 2-hour surge: +1,500 max HP, Regain 5 TP/tick, plus Refresh and Regen scaled to your max MP/HP. A daily reason to log in, and a head start on your next climb.

This page is generated directly from the live Apex Trials and Paragon configuration — every number above always matches the server.

docs.title: Casino — Lady Luck
docs.text:
Feeling lucky? Lady Luck runs a four-game casino in GM Home where you can gamble your gil on slots, high-low, roulette, and dice. Every game keeps a small house edge, so over time it's a gil sink — but a hot streak can pay out huge, and any single win big enough is shouted to the whole server.

Summary

A four-game gil-sink casino — slots, high-low, roulette, and dice — run by Lady Luck in GM Home. Pick a stake and play; the biggest wins shout server-wide.

docs.title: Where to play
docs.text: Lady Luck holds court in GM Home — step up to the table, pick a game, and place your stake.

docs.title: Placing a bet
docs.text:
Bets are fixed tiers (the menu can't take a typed-in amount) — pick your stake, then your game:

Stakes: 5,000 / 25,000 / 100,000 / 500,000 gil.

Any single win of 2,000,000 gil or more is shouted server-wide — bragging rights included.

docs.title: The games
docs.text:
Game How it works Payouts House edge Slots Spin three reels, match three symbols 7×3 = 150×, Bell×3 = 30×, Melon×3 = 10×, Cherry×3 = 4× ~8.4% High-Low A card 1–13 is shown; bet whether the next is higher or lower Odds-based — safe calls pay barely over 1×, long shots pay big ~8.0% Roulette Single-zero wheel (0–36); bet a colour/odd/even or a single number Even-money 2×, single number 35× ~2.7% even / ~5.4% single Dice Roll 2d6; bet the High (8–12) / Low (2–6) band or Lucky 7 High/Low 2.25×, Lucky 7 5× ~6.2% band / ~16.7% on 7

All payouts are total-return multipliers: a 2× win on a 25,000 gil bet returns 50,000 (a net gain of 25,000), a push returns your bet, and a loss keeps it. The house edge is the long-run cost of playing — small on the even-money bets, bigger on the long-shots that pay the most.

docs.title: Chocobo Derby
docs.text:
Down in GM Home, the Race Caller runs the races. Put gil on a runner and watch it play out — and if you've raised a chocobo of your own that's tough enough, line it up at the gate and bet on yourself.

Summary

Bet gil on chocobo races at the Race Caller in GM Home; raise a strong enough chocobo of your own and you can enter it as a runner for a bigger payout.

docs.title: Where to play
docs.text: The Race Caller stands in the activities row of GM Home. Step up to check the odds board, place a bet, and watch the race play out.

docs.title: Placing a bet
docs.text:
Stakes: 10,000 / 50,000 / 250,000 gil.

Each runner carries odds set by its hidden strength: the long-shots pay the most, the favourites the least. The house keeps about 15% of the fair payout as its cut, and even a heavy favourite always returns at least 1.15× your stake when it wins. Back the wrong bird and you lose your bet.

docs.title: The field
docs.text:
Every race fields 6 runners. If you aren't racing a chocobo of your own, they're all from the house stable; if you are, your bird takes one of the gates. The stable regulars are drawn from this roster:

  • Chocofury · Bolt v. Kweh · Lady Bolt
  • Sir Scratch · Meteor Mike · Yellowcomet
  • Dust Dan · Sandy Sally · Gallop Gus
  • Wark Wonder · Featherluck · Kwehsar

A race runs about 20 seconds of live commentary before the winner crosses the line.

docs.title: Racing your own chocobo
docs.text:
Raised a chocobo of your own? Once it reaches the adolescent stage (or older) you can enter it as a runner instead of just betting on the stable.

Your bird races on its real ability — its strength, endurance, and how much affection you've raised it with all feed its hidden racing form, so a well-loved, well-trained chocobo genuinely out-classes the house runners and races at shorter odds.

And there's a reason to root for your own: winning a race on your chocobo pays an extra 25% on top of the normal payout.

Like the casino, the derby is a long-run gil sink — the house keeps its cut over time — but a well-judged bet, or a champion bird of your own, can still pay off big on the day.

docs.title: Colosseum — Ranked Arena
docs.text:
Think you're the strongest champion on the server? Enroll at the Arena Herald in GM Home and prove it. The Colosseum is an asynchronous, ranked PvP-style arena: you duel level-scaled replicas of other champions to climb an Elo rating ladder — no need to catch your rivals online.

Summary

A ranked arena in GM Home where you duel AI replicas of other champions to climb an Elo ladder, earning Hunt Marks for every win.

docs.title: Where to fight
docs.text:
The Arena Herald stands in GM Home — talk to them to enroll your champion on the ladder, browse the roster of rivals, and accept a duel.

Enrolling snapshots your champion's name, race, job, and level onto the ladder. From then on, anyone can challenge a replica of your champion — and you can challenge theirs — at any time.

docs.title: How a duel works
docs.text:
When you challenge a champion, you fight a level-scaled replica of them — an AI stand-in, so the rival doesn't need to be online.

  • A 3-second countdown gives you a moment to ready up before the replica appears.
  • You have 5 minutes to win. Run out the clock and the duel is forfeit.
  • You can challenge each champion once per day (resets at 00:00 UTC) — pick your matches and come back tomorrow for a rematch.

Duels are fought in GM Home, with the replica spawning right next to you. There's no party play here — it's a one-on-one test of your champion.

docs.title: The rating ladder
docs.text:
Every champion starts at a rating of 1,200 and can never fall below 800. Win a duel and your rating climbs while your opponent's slips; the ladder is zero-sum, so the only way up is through other champions.

A replica scales to the rival's rating, not their gear — a higher-rated champion is proof of a dangerous fighter. The tougher the rating, the higher the replica's level (from 99 up to a cap of 205) and the deeper its HP pool (2× to 10× a normal mob's health). Climbing the ladder literally makes your own champion harder for others to beat.

Because the ladder is zero-sum, ratings stay honest and self-balancing: there's always a beatable opponent near the bottom and a fearsome one at the top. Your current and best ratings, wins, and losses are all tracked for the leaderboards.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Duels pay out in Hunt Marks, the server's main currency:

  • Win: 10 marks — plus a bonus for punching up and beating a higher-rated champion.
  • Loss: 25 marks as a consolation, so a defeat is never a total loss.

The bigger the gap when you beat someone rated above you, the sweeter the haul — the ladder rewards bravery as much as skill.

docs.title: Dynamis — Divergence
docs.text:
A custom take on Dynamis built for the relaunch. Each of the four nations has a Divergence Portal at its old Dynamis entrance that tears open an alternate-timeline instance. Pay a single Dynamis currency, step through — solo is fine — and fight through escalating waves of Beastmen to fell the zone's Mega-Boss. Clearing a zone unlocks one Reforge slot, and the medals you farm inside let the Divergence Smith push your Reforged Artifact, Relic, and Empyrean armor up the +1 → +2 → +3 ladder.

Summary

Four city Dynamis instances reached through entry portals for one Dynamis currency each. Clear the waves to unlock armor slots and farm medals, then reforge AF/Relic/Empyrean gear +1 → +2 → +3 at the Divergence Smith in San d'Oria.

docs.title: Getting in
docs.text:
A Divergence Portal stands at each city's Dynamis entrance. Trade the toll, confirm, and you're warped — solo is fine — into that city's alternate-timeline instance:

Portal Unlocks (Reforge slot) San d'Oria [D] Feet Bastok [D] Hands Windurst [D] Head Jeuno [D] Legs

Entry toll: a One Byne Bill per run.

docs.title: How a run plays out
docs.text:
Each run is a timed push through escalating waves. The clock can be extended by clearing optional targets, up to a hard cap of 120 minutes:

  1. Wave 1 — Squadron. Trash mobs, optional time-extension statues (each one felled adds +1 min), and the Mid-Boss.
  2. Wave 2 — Regiment. Felling the Mid-Boss advances the wave (+30 min): fresh trash plus the Mega-Boss.
  3. Wave 3 — The Disjoined. In zones that have one, the Disjoined NM manifests at the elemental circle after the Mega-Boss falls. No more time can be gained here — finish it to win.

Clearing the run unlocks that city's Reforge slot. Beastmen's, Kindred's, and Demon's Medals drop from the mobs inside — bank them for the smith.

docs.title: Reforging your armor
docs.text:
Clear a city's zone to unlock its armor slot; clear all four to unlock Body. Then bring the Divergence Smith in Southern San d'Oria a Reforged Artifact, Relic, or Empyrean piece and the medals to push it up a tier — +1 → +2 → +3.

Slots, and the city that unlocks each:

Slot Unlocked by Head Windurst [D] Hands Bastok [D] Legs Jeuno [D] Feet San d'Oria [D] Body Clearing all four city zones

Medal cost per upgrade:

Upgrade Cost → +2 3× Beastmen's Medal → +3 3× Kindred's Medal, 1× Demon's Medal

The smith only takes pieces for a slot you've already unlocked, and only when you're holding the full medal cost — trade a reforged piece to push it one tier higher.

docs.title: The Endless Tower
docs.text:
A spire with no roof, only more floors. The Endless Tower is a solo gauntlet that climbs through ever-stronger monsters, a boss waiting on every tenth floor. Fight your way to the top and the Pinnacle Sovereign falls — and with it, a piece of your Prime Weapon legend. One death, and the run is over.

Summary

A solo 50-floor climb from the Endless Tower Arbiter in GM Home — a boss every 10 floors, no Trusts allowed, one death ends the run, and reaching floor 50 completes Prime Weapon Trial 2.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
Speak to the Tower Climb in GM Home and choose Enter the Tower to be warped into Walk Of Echoes. After a short breather the first floor spawns, and each cleared floor leads straight into the next.

This is a solo gauntlet — Trusts are disabled inside the Tower. A single death ends the run on the spot with no reward and no floor saved, so you only ever advance by surviving. You can bail out early at any time with !tower abort, and !tower on its own reports your current floor (or your best-ever floor when you're not in a run).

docs.title: How the floors scale
docs.text:
The Tower is 50 floors tall. Every floor throws a pack of monsters at you; clear them all and the next floor spawns after a brief pause. Monsters get a fresh, larger level the deeper you climb, and the pack grows from 3 monsters on the lowest floors toward a bigger crowd near the top.

Floors are grouped into ten-floor bands, each a sharp step up in monster level:

Floors Monster level 1–10 120 11–20 155 21–30 185 31–40 215 41–50 240

docs.title: Bosses
docs.text:
Every 10th floor is a boss floor: a single towering monster stands between you and the next band. Each boss rolls one random affix when it appears, so the same boss can play very differently from run to run.

The bosses, band by band:

Floor Boss Level HP 10 Guardian of the Spire 135 600,000 20 Shadow of the Abyss 170 1,200,000 30 The Eternal Warden 205 2,500,000 40 Lord of the Void 240 4,000,000 50 The Pinnacle Sovereign 250 7,000,000

Possible boss affixes:

  • Fortified
  • Frenzied
  • Regenerating
  • Empowered
  • Colossal
  • Furious

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
The Tower's prize is the climb itself. Reaching floor 50 and defeating The Pinnacle Sovereign completes Prime Weapon Trial 2 — the gateway to forging your Prime Weapon at the Prime Armory. The trial only needs to be cleared once; after that, floor 50 is pure bragging rights.

Your deepest floor ever cleared is tracked as a personal best, so even a run that ends short of the top still pushes your record on the leaderboard. There are no checkpoints — the Tower only remembers how high you climbed.

Climb carefully — there is no checkpoint, no party to lean on, and the Tower only remembers how high you dared to go.

docs.title: High-Tier Battlefields
docs.text:
The High-Tier Battlefields (HTBF) bring the classic mission boss fights back as repeatable, scaled endgame content. Each battlefield is a retail story-boss encounter — Avatar Primes, the Chains of Promathia bosses, the Ark Angels, and more — rebuilt with three difficulty tiers so you can climb from a warm-up clear to a genuine wall.

Entry is gated by a Phantom Gem key item, bought for gil from a vendor in Leafallia. Buy the gem for the fight you want, trade it at that battlefield's entrance, and choose your tier. Clears pay out gil and Hunt Marks that scale with the tier, plus a chance at retail-style spoils from the treasure chest.

Summary

Repeatable, tier-scaled versions of the classic mission boss battlefields. Buy a Phantom Gem with gil in Leafallia, trade it at the battlefield entrance, pick a tier (I / II / III), and win for scaling gil + Hunt Mark rewards.

docs.title: Getting in
docs.text:
Buy your Phantom Gem from the Phantom Gems vendor in Leafallia (the relaunch hub). Each gem is a key item bought with gil; the vendor's menu is grouped by expansion so you can browse the full roster. Once you hold a gem, travel to that battlefield's zone, trade the gem at the entrance, and pick a difficulty tier (I / II / III).

You can only hold one gem of a given type at a time, and entering a battlefield consumes it -- buy a fresh gem for each attempt.

docs.title: Scheduled Invasions — Defend Al Zahbi
docs.text:
Eight times a day the Voidsent pour into Al Zahbi, and it falls to whoever's around to throw them back. Invasions are a Besieged-style outpost defense: escalating waves of enemies that grow with the size of your defending force, capped off by a boss. Survive the assault and every defender shares in the spoils.

Summary

An eight-times-daily Besieged-style defense of Al Zahbi — waves of Voidsent that scale with how many defenders show up, ending in a boss, rewarding marks and Infamy to all who hold the line.

docs.title: When it happens
docs.text:
The Voidsent strike 8 times a day, at 00:00 UTC and 03:00 UTC and 06:00 UTC and 09:00 UTC and 12:00 UTC and 15:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC and 21:00 UTC.

  • A server-wide warning shouts 5 minutes before each window so you can rally at Al Zahbi.
  • The assault only fires if at least one defender is standing in Al Zahbi when the window opens — it stays armed for up to 10 minutes waiting for someone to show. No defenders, no invasion.

Just be in Al Zahbi when a window opens and you're automatically a defender — there's nothing to sign up for.

docs.title: The waves
docs.text:
The assault rolls in as a ladder of escalating waves, each tougher than the last, before the Voidsent commander itself appears:

Wave Enemy level Vanguard 110 Shock Troops 125 Dreadguard 140 Apex Guard 155 The Warlord 165 Voidsent Warlord (boss) 175

The final wave brings its own trash alongside the boss — clear them all and the boss to win.

docs.title: Scaling and time limit
docs.text: The more defenders who answer the call, the larger each wave — bring friends and the horde swells to match. The whole assault, from the first wave to the boss, must be cleared within 15 minutes. Hold the line and fell the boss before the clock runs out to claim victory.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Every defender present is paid out — credit goes to anyone in Al Zahbi at the relevant moment:

  • 20 Hunt Marks for each wave cleared.
  • 100 Hunt Marks + 100 Infamy on a full victory (the boss falls). This is a major source of Infamy.
  • 150 Hunt Marks as a consolation if the clock beats the defense.

Victory also drops gear-vendor medals — a guaranteed Kindreds Medal haul, plus a guaranteed Demons Medal drop.

Those medals feed the Armor and Weapons gear vendors (see the !hunt gear loop), so a strong turnout at invasions is a steady route to better equipment.

docs.title: Job Mastery
docs.text:
The final proof of mastery is to stand alone against a weapon's living avatar. Each weapon type has a Guardian — a single, brutal boss you face solo in Walk Of Echoes. Beat the Guardian of any weapon and you complete the last trial on the Prime Weapon path.

Summary

Pick a weapon type at the Weapon Mastery Sage in GM Home, fight its Guardian solo in Walk Of Echoes, and a single victory completes Trial 4 of the Prime Weapon path. Death ends the attempt with no reward.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: Find the Weapon Mastery Sage in GM Home and pick a weapon type. Choosing one warps you alone into Walk Of Echoes, where that weapon's Guardian appears moments later. There is no quest and no cost to attempt a challenge — just talk to the Sage and choose. If you ever need to bail out of an active attempt, use !mastery abort.

docs.title: The Guardian fights
docs.text:
There is one Guardian for each of the 12 weapon types. Each is a solo fight — trusts are disabled in the arena, so it is you and your weapon against the Guardian. Whichever one you defeat, the credit is the same; pick the weapon type you fight best with.

Every Guardian rolls a random affix when it spawns, so the same fight plays differently each attempt. They hit hard and carry an enormous health pool — bring your strongest setup.

Death ends the challenge with no reward and no save: you are returned to GM Home and must start over.

Weapon type Guardian Sword Guardian of the Blade Dagger Guardian of the Shadow Grt.Sword Guardian of Ruin Axe Guardian of the Axe Grt.Axe Guardian of the Vanguard Scythe Guardian of Catastrophe Polearm Guardian of the Dragon Katana Void Blade Guardian Grt.Katana Guardian of the Kensei Club Guardian of the Mace Staff Guardian of Elements Archery Guardian of the Hunt

docs.title: Affixes
docs.text:
When a Guardian appears it carries one of these affixes, rolled at random and shown to you as it spawns. Every affix piles real offense on top of the Guardian's base power, so there is no "safe" roll:

Affix Fortified Frenzied Regenerating Empowered Colossal Furious

docs.title: Reward
docs.text:
Defeating any Guardian completes Trial 4 of the Prime Weapon path — the final gate before the Prime Armory will forge your Prime weapon. You only need to beat one Guardian to earn that credit.

Beyond that first clear, every additional Guardian you defeat is tracked on its own, so completionists can work through all 12 weapon types — but a single victory is all Trial 4 requires.

Job Mastery is the capstone of the Prime Weapon journey — there is no party to hide behind and no second chance once you fall, so master your weapon before you challenge its Guardian.

docs.title: Maat's Challenge
docs.text:
Think you can take on the master? Seek out Maat's Echo in Ru'Lude Gardens and pay your Infamy for a chance to fight a level-250 incarnation of Maat in the very arena where the Genkai trials once took place — Waughroon Shrine. Win, and there's a chance he'll leave behind something that could change the outcome of your next augment.

Summary

Talk to Maat's Echo in Ru'Lude Gardens, pay 150 Infamy, and you'll be teleported to Waughroon Shrine to face a level-250 Maat — now the single hardest fight on the server, tuned above the endgame Ascension bosses. Defeat him for a 25% chance at a Maat's Blessing — an item that guarantees your next augment at the Augment Moogle will be a critical. He also has a 0.5% chance to drop a Prime Voucher (Prime Weapon Trial 3).

Stat Value Entry cost 150 Infamy Maat's level 200 Maat's Blessing drop chance 25% Entry NPC Maat's Echo — Ru'Lude Gardens Fight zone Waughroon Shrine Simultaneous fights Unlimited — every challenger gets their own

docs.title: Where to find the NPC
docs.text: Maat's Echo stands near the original Maat NPC in Ru'Lude Gardens, just to the side of the familiar old sage. Look for the gold star icon.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Talk to Maat's Echo and accept the challenge.
  2. The cost is 150 Infamy. If your Infamy is short, come back when you've earned more.
  3. You're immediately transported to Waughroon Shrine — the very battlefield where Genkai trials were once decided.
  4. Maat appears before you at level 250 with a stat block tuned above our toughest Ascension boss: brutal melee, accuracy that punches through tank gear, and Chainspell nukes that delete the careless — come prepared.
  5. On death, Maat has a 25% chance to drop Maat's Blessing.

Bring a crowd

Every challenger gets their own Maat, claim-locked to them — many people can fight in the shrine at the same time without interfering. Your Maat is yours alone; no one else can tag it, steal it, or help kill it. If you leave or die, your Maat despawns on its own after about 45 seconds.

docs.title: The reward: Maat's Blessing
docs.text:
Maat's Blessing is a rare, EX item — it cannot be auctioned, traded, or stored.

When you hold Maat's Blessing in your inventory and trade gear + catalysts to the Augment Moogle, your augment is guaranteed to be a critical — the 2× multiplier applies automatically, no roll required.

The item is consumed on success. It is not consumed if the augment fails (e.g. you cancel, or your inventory is full).

How critical augments work

A critical augment doubles the exdata boost applied to every catalyst in that trade. Normally this relies on your Augment Sage rank and a random roll — Maat's Blessing bypasses that entirely. See Augment Moogle and Augment Sage for the full system details.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Come geared. Maat carries an explicit Lv250 stat block cranked above the endgame Ascension bosses — his attacks, spell damage, and HP all reflect it. This is not a casual fight.
  • Watch your MP. Maat's RDM incarnation uses Chainspell + high-tier nukes. Magic defense, Stoneskin, and Utsusemi all help buy time.
  • You keep the Infamy on his death. Only the entry fee is spent; you don't lose more if you die.
  • If you die or leave without killing him, your Maat despawns after a short lull. The 150 Infamy entry cost is still spent — don't go in unprepared.
  • Stack up before augmenting. Maat's Blessing lasts indefinitely while held. You can earn multiple blessings before redeeming them, but the item is RARE so you can only hold one at a time.

docs.title: Provisioners' League
docs.text:
A non-combat league for anglers and crafters. The League Steward at Reisenjima Henge tracks your fishing weigh-ins and high-quality craft turn-ins, awarding League Points that climb a five-rank ladder — and every rank-up permanently boosts the marks you earn around the server.

Summary

Fish and turn in HQ crafts at the League Steward in Reisenjima Henge to earn League Points; climbing the five-rank ladder grants a permanent, stacking mark bonus.

docs.title: Where to join
docs.text: Seek out the League Steward at Reisenjima Henge — he keeps the books for both anglers and crafters. Talk to him to check your rank, your League Point total, and this week's featured fish.

docs.title: Earning League Points
docs.text:
There are two ways to earn League Points:

Fishing weigh-ins — every fish you catch is worth points that scale with the fish's skill: the tougher the catch, the more it pays. On top of that:

  • A big fish (the ruler-measured monsters) is worth 2× points.
  • A legendary catch is league gold — worth 10× points.
  • This week's featured fish pays a 3× bonus — a rotating target that keeps the weekly race fresh and is always something a normal angler can land.

Crafting turn-ins — every high-quality (HQ) item you hand in at the server's Crafting Exchange also credits League Points alongside its usual reward, so your crafting progress counts here too.

There's also a weekly leaderboard scored on the points you earn that week — a fresh race every week, separate from your lifetime total.

docs.title: The rank ladder
docs.text:
Your lifetime League Points decide your rank. Each rank you reach grants a permanent mark bonus that stacks as you climb — reaching a higher rank keeps every bonus below it.

Rank League Points Mark bonus Apprentice Provisioner — — Journeyman Provisioner 750 +250 Expert Provisioner 2,500 +750 Master Provisioner 7,500 +2,000 Legendary Provisioner 20,000 +5,000

docs.title: Seasonal Events
docs.text:
From time to time — around holidays and special occasions — the server runs a seasonal event that boosts the marks you earn from Hunting League kills. During an event window, every qualifying kill pays a mark multiplier on top of your usual amount, for a limited time.

Summary

During a seasonal event, Hunting League kills earn bonus marks (a mark multiplier) for a limited time. Check below to see whether one is running.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When an event is live, the bonus is fully automatic — just keep hunting. Each event has:

  • A name that appears in the kill bonus message so you know it's active.
  • A mark multiplier (for example, 2× for double marks or 1.5× for a 50% bonus) applied on top of any Hunter's Guild amplifier you've already earned.
  • A start and end time in UTC. The bonus only applies to kills made inside that window.

Only one event bonus applies at a time, so you always get the best multiplier that's currently running.

docs.text:
No seasonal event is running right now — check back around holidays!

docs.title: The Star-Devourer — Weekly Raid Boss
docs.text:
The ultimate test on the Relaunch server: a colossal, multi-phase raid boss lurking at the Voidgate in Escha-RuAun. The Star-Devourer is a server-shared fight anyone can join, but its richest rewards are locked to once per week — so rally a raid, learn the dance, and bring it down.

Summary

A weekly-lockout, multi-phase raid boss (The Star-Devourer) at Escha-RuAun — survive the stance dance, the tendril adds, the dispel sweep, and the enrage for marks and Infamy once a week.

docs.title: Starting the fight
docs.text: Seek out the Voidgate Sentinel in Escha-RuAun, standing beside the Voidspire Warden. Speak to them to summon The Star-Devourer — the fight is server-shared, so anyone in the area can join the brawl. It's a true raid: bring a crowd.

docs.title: The boss
docs.text: The Star-Devourer is a level 200 behemoth with a colossal health pool — roughly 45× a normal boss's HP. This is a long, phase-driven endurance fight, not a quick burn — expect to work through every stage below.

docs.title: Fight mechanics
docs.text:
The Star-Devourer is a scripted encounter — its phases fire in a fixed order as you chip away at its health. Knowing what's coming is the difference between a clean kill and a wipe.

The stance dance — from 90% HP. Once the boss drops to 90% it begins alternating between two stances roughly every 45 seconds:

  • Aegis Stance — blades glance off (near-immune to physical), but magic rips through.
  • Umbral Stance — spells gutter out (near-immune to magic), but steel bites deep.

Watch the on-screen call-out and switch your damage type to match, or your numbers will vanish.

The tendrils — at 75% and 30% HP. The Devourer spawns Starspawn Tendrils and starts rapidly healing itself while they live — the tendrils feed the maw. Cut them down fast to stop the heal and resume your assault.

Dispel sweep — at 50% HP. A wave of unbeing strips protective buffs from everyone engaged. Be ready to re-buff and press on.

Final fury — at 15% HP. The boss permanently spikes its attack and attack speed for the last stretch — the closing burn is a dangerous one.

Soft enrage — 12 minutes in. If the fight drags on this long, a massive permanent buff lands and the encounter becomes a race. Kill it before the clock turns the Devourer untouchable.

If every living raider leaves the boss's area for too long, the fight resets and the Devourer despawns — keep someone on it.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Rewards are on a weekly lockout (resetting Monday 00:00 UTC):

  • First kill of the week: 2,500 Hunt Marks + 500 Infamy.
  • Repeat kills the same week: 250 Hunt Marks as a consolation, so it's always worth helping your friends down it again.

You must be near the boss when it dies to get credit.

The weekly reset shares the same Monday 00:00 UTC anchor as the Weekly Hunt Board and the weekly Raid, so you can plan your big-ticket weekly runs together.
